ammunition.topic: Tilted / two-frame 'dipole cosmology' as a non-kinematic cosmic-dipole source (rescues the tilted-cosmology motivation the audit stripped)
ammunition.finding: Krishnan, Mondol & Sheikh-Jabbari formalized the 'dipole cosmological principle' — the maximally-Copernican generalization of FLRW that admits a cosmic flow (tilt). The Einstein equations become four ODEs (not two Friedmann equations) describing an axisymmetric, tilted Bianchi V / VII_h geometry with an anisotropic scale factor (breaking SO(3)->U(1)) plus a tilt function; cosmic flow can accelerate even while metric shear decays. Their companion 'tilt instability' paper proves FLRW is unstable to growth of fluid-flow (tilt) anisotropies even during accelerated expansion, and that this matter-sector instability is INVISIBLE to cosmic-no-hair arguments (which only bound metric shear). This is precisely a modern, GR-consistent realization of a global tilt sourcing a cosmic dipole.
references: Krishnan, Mondol, Sheikh-Jabbari 2023, 'Dipole Cosmology: The Copernican Paradigm Beyond FLRW', JCAP 07 (2023) 020, arXiv:2209.14918, https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.14918
Krishnan, Mondol, Sheikh-Jabbari 2023, 'A tilt instability in the cosmological principle', Eur. Phys. J. C 83, 874 (2023), arXiv:2211.08093, https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.08093
Allali, Sheikh-Jabbari et al. 2025, 'Big Bang in dipole cosmology', Eur. Phys. J. C (2025), arXiv:2307.15791, https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.15791
ammunition.rescue_leverage: Directly answers D-THEORY-PROVENANCE-OWNERSHIP: the tilt is a first-class dynamical degree of freedom with its own field equations, not an ad hoc overload of Omega_tilt. The tilt-instability theorem gives an independent, published reason why a global tilt need NOT track shear — so the audit's demand that a global-tilt claim reduce to a shear/geometry detection is too strong; tilt and shear are separately excitable. Reframes the program's Bianchi V/VII_h + tilt target as the exact object KMS study, giving the pre-solver methods paper a live, citable physical target rather than an abandoned one.

ammunition.topic: Frame-dependence of the deceleration parameter and peculiar-velocity 'tilt' effects on cosmographic observables (Tsagas lineage)
ammunition.finding: Tsagas and collaborators show that a realistic observer with a peculiar (tilt) velocity relative to the smooth Hubble flow measures a DIFFERENT deceleration parameter than the fundamental frame, purely from relative-motion terms that enter at LINEAR order in the peculiar velocity; at a critical scale the locally measured q can flip sign (apparent acceleration) while the global universe decelerates. The 2024 extension to perturbed Bianchi backgrounds finds the qualitative effect survives, dominated by the tilt rather than by background shear unless anisotropy is unrealistically large.

ammunition.rescue_leverage: Ammunition against D-THEORY-COEFFICIENT-REGRESSIONS and the 'linear vs quadratic Omega_tilt overload' charge: the literature establishes that tilt enters distinct observables at distinct orders — LINEAR in v for the dipole/aberration and deceleration-parameter shift, QUADRATIC in v for the quadrupole/shear-like imprint. ammunition.topic: Observational status of the cosmic (matter) dipole anomaly — the empirical motivation for a tilt/anisotropy program
ammunition.finding: The number-count dipole of radio (NVSS) and mid-IR (CatWISE) sources aligns in direction with the CMB dipole but has ~2x the amplitude expected from pure kinematics, with joint significance quoted >5 sigma (Secrest et al.); the 2025 Rev. Mod. Phys. colloquium frames this as: either the matter and radiation rest-frames differ, or there is intrinsic anisotropy in at least one — a direct challenge to FLRW. HOWEVER, DESI DR1 quasars (1.18M QSO) yield |v| = 443.8 +/- 204.1 km/s, consistent with the kinematic 370 km/s at 1.56 sigma, and CatWISE 'cosmic glitch'/clustering reassessments argue systematics inflate the anomaly. The anomaly is real in some catalogues and contested in others.

ammunition.topic: Converse of almost-EGS: an almost-isotropic CMB temperature does NOT imply an almost-FLRW universe (direct counter to D-THEORY-FLRW-EGS-SEMANTICS)
ammunition.finding: Nilsson, Uggla, Wainwright & Lim exhibit spatially-homogeneous (Bianchi) models in which the CMB temperature anisotropy sits within observational limits yet the Weyl curvature is NOT small — the models are far from FLRW despite an almost-isotropic sky temperature. The distinction is between anisotropy of the expansion versus intrinsic anisotropy of the gravitational (Weyl) field; small dipole/quadrupole temperature constrains the former far more tightly than the latter. This is a rigorous, published counterexample to using CMB near-isotropy as a sufficient FLRW premise.
references: Nilsson, Uggla, Wainwright, Lim 1999, 'An almost isotropic cosmic microwave temperature does not imply an almost isotropic universe', ApJ 522, L1-L3, arXiv:astro-ph/9904252, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9904252
Related construction: 'Anisotropic universes with isotropic cosmic microwave background radiation', arXiv:gr-qc/9912001, https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9912001
ammunition.rescue_leverage: This is the strongest single rescue for the theory axis. The audit's D-THEORY-FLRW-EGS-SEMANTICS ruling ('x_C=0 / repaired frame condition incorrectly used as sufficient FLRW/EGS premises; repository counterexamples defeat the converse') is EXACTLY the Nilsson et al. finding — but published and peer-reviewed. ammunition.topic: Generalized EGS theorems and the acceleration/geodesic gap (the precise hypothesis the converse needs)
ammunition.finding: Clarkson & Barrett found the complete class of irrotational perfect-fluid spacetimes admitting an exactly isotropic radiation field for every fundamental observer, showing they form a subclass of the thermodynamic Stephani universes and reduce to FLRW if and only if the four-acceleration vanishes (equivalently the flow is geodesic). Isotropic radiation therefore permits a one-parameter family of inhomogeneous, accelerating (non-geodesic) models; FLRW-uniqueness is recovered only after adding the geodesic/zero-acceleration premise. Later work ('More on the EGS theorem') extended this to the almost-isotropic, Copernican-principle setting.
references: Clarkson & Barrett 1999, 'Does the isotropy of the CMB imply a homogeneous universe? Some generalized EGS theorems', Class. Quantum Grav. 16, 3781, https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/16/12/302

ammunition.topic: Maartens-Ellis-Stoeger CMB bound hierarchy on shear, vorticity, four-acceleration and Weyl (topic c lineage + modern order-counting)
ammunition.finding: MES derived explicit inequalities bounding present-day shear (Sigma_0 < ~1e-4), vorticity, Weyl parameter (W_0 < ~1e-3) and density gradients directly from CMB quadrupole/octupole limits, assuming only a (partially testable) weak Copernican principle rather than a priori homogeneity. The framework treats the multipole-to-kinematic map order by order, so the dipole constrains velocity/tilt at linear order while quadrupole/octupole constrain shear and Weyl at quadratic order — a clean separation of which anisotropy variable each multipole sees.

ammunition.topic: The classical coupled VII_h temperature template is only a subset of the full linearized Bianchi freedom (topic d — rescues the abandoned VII_h and the isotropy-null limitation)
ammunition.finding: Pontzen's 'rogues gallery' computes the FULL linearized dynamical freedom of homogeneous-anisotropic (Bianchi) CMB patterns and shows the classical coupled temperature template (the Barrow-Juszkiewicz-Sonoda / Jaffe-type single-mode spiral used in WMAP/Planck Bianchi fits) is only one slice of a much larger mode space. Some modes hide in superhorizon perturbations at early times (evading BBN bounds) yet produce nontrivial z=0 temperature AND polarization patterns. Pontzen & Challinor further derived the Bianchi polarization signature (efficient E->B conversion, parity-violating TB/EB), extending the template beyond temperature alone.

The advocate should NOT re-adopt the abandoned classical coupled template but instead pivot to Pontzen's full mode space + Pontzen-Challinor polarization as the correct target, arguing that Planck/Saadeh nulls tested only the restricted template and are therefore non-exhaustive. ammunition.topic: Modern model-conditional isotropy bounds and their template-dependence (Saadeh et al.)
ammunition.finding: Saadeh, Feeney, Pontzen, Peiris & McEwen performed the first simultaneous Bayesian test of all anisotropic-expansion (Bianchi) degrees of freedom against Planck, finding anisotropy disfavored at 121000:1 and bounding the shear-to-expansion rate to <~1e-9 (rotation <~1e-9 rad/yr). Crucially, the constraint is stated within a specified physical model class (Bianchi VII_h-type expansion anisotropy with a chosen vorticity treatment); it is model-conditional, and does not constrain intrinsic-Weyl or superhorizon-hidden modes that produce sub-threshold temperature signatures.
references: Saadeh, Feeney, Pontzen, Peiris, McEwen 2016, 'How Isotropic is the Universe?', Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 131302, arXiv:1605.07178, https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.07178
ammunition.rescue_leverage: Two-edged and used honestly: the advocate concedes Saadeh as the strongest modern isotropy bound (this is what the isotropy advocate correctly upheld) BUT cites Nilsson-Uggla-Wainwright-Lim + Pontzen to argue it is model-conditional and template-restricted, so it constrains rather than closes the weak-anisotropy programme. This is the calibrated, both-poles-honest framing the referees demanded, and it justifies the program's 'model-conditional cross-check' claim tier for K5/Saadeh comparisons that the audit already tolerated.

ammunition.topic: Backreaction / averaging origin of large-scale tilt + Bianchi-like anisotropy from nonlinear structure (Buchert lineage, topic a: tilt+curvature)
ammunition.finding: Anton & Clifton derive, by decomposing fields about a preferred spatial direction and averaging, effective large-scale field equations that — up to backreaction terms — take the form of locally-rotationally-symmetric Bianchi cosmologies, and applied them to the dust Farnsworth solutions that support BOTH anisotropic expansion and a large-scale bulk flow (tilt). Independently, Buchert-lineage curvature-averaging work (Mourier-Heinesen foliation dependence; Williams-Buchert-lineage local-universe averaging) finds no convergence of the averaged energy budget to a flat-LCDM background within ~300 Mpc/h, consistent with persistent bulk flows. Together these give a structure-formation mechanism by which an effective global tilt + emergent curvature can arise without a fundamental Bianchi metric.

ammunition.topic: Model-independent anisotropic cosmography: general multipole degrees of freedom as the honest FLRW-test object (Heinesen)
ammunition.finding: Heinesen derived the luminosity-distance 'Hubble law' to third order in redshift for a GENERAL spacetime with no metric or field-equation assumption, showing the anisotropic expansion is captured by a finite set of physically interpretable multipole coefficients (9, 25, 61 degrees of freedom at O(z), O(z^2), O(z^3)). This yields direction-dependent effective H_0, q_0, curvature and jerk that can be measured model-independently and directly test the FLRW ansatz; Heinesen & Macpherson and CF4-based follow-ups estimate the expected dominant dipole (in q) and quadrupole (in H) multipoles for the local volume.

ammunition.rescue_leverage: Gives the program a model-independent, frame-explicit language for Omega_tilt-type observables that sidesteps D-THEORY-PROVENANCE-OWNERSHIP overloading: the tilt/dipole is one identifiable multipole DoF among a finite, published basis, so local-linear (dipole) vs global-quadratic (quadrupole/shear) meanings map onto DISTINCT cosmographic coefficients rather than one ambiguous symbol. ammunition.topic: Pontzen-Challinor semi-analytic near-FRW Bianchi multipole hierarchy + polarization templates
ammunition.finding: Pontzen & Challinor (2007) derived the CMB radiative-transfer equation for nearly-FRW Bianchi universes as a lightweight multipole hierarchy that adds proper recombination, reionization, and — crucially — POLARIZATION (E, B, TB/EB parity) to the VIIh temperature templates. Peak polarization ~1.2 uK, confined to ell<10. This is a specialized, published, order-reduced hierarchy (not a bespoke general Boltzmann code) and it supplies falsifiable T+E+B+parity predictions per Bianchi model. ammunition.topic: ANICOSMO full-degrees-of-freedom Bayesian model selection (scalar/vector/tensor) with nested sampling
ammunition.finding: Saadeh, Feeney, Pontzen, Peiris & McEwen (2016) built ANICOSMO: a nested-sampling (MultiNest) Bayesian framework that, for the first time, constrains ALL homogeneous anisotropic degrees of freedom (scalar, vector, tensor modes) using Planck T+E, with Bianchi VIIh as the parent class and 'other types obtained by taking suitable limits.' ammunition.topic: Template-bank / matched-filter geometry discrimination with Bayesian evidence — the mature published method

ammunition.topic: BipoSH / minimal-BipoSH forward models linking anisotropic covariance to observable off-diagonal signatures
ammunition.finding: Bipolar spherical harmonics expand the full two-point covariance <a_lm a_l'm'*> into a complete orthogonal basis; nonzero BipoSH coefficients A^{LM}_{ll'} are the model-independent signature of statistical-isotropy violation. Recent work (Dipanshu, Karan & Souradeep 2024, 'minimal BipoSH') gives closed-form estimators isolating L=1,2 SI-violation (hemispherical asymmetry, non-circular beam), and generalized isotropic angular correlation functions (Adhikari et al. 2023) capture SI violation without a power spectrum. These are DATA-SIDE estimators/forward models with analytic mask coupling — no Boltzmann solver.

ammunition.topic: Simulation-based inference / emulator model selection on precomputed template maps
ammunition.finding: Simulation-based inference (SBI) performs Bayesian parameter estimation AND model comparison when the likelihood is intractable, using only forward simulations. Cole et al. (2022, TMNRE) demonstrated converged CMB posteriors with orders of magnitude fewer simulator calls than MCMC; sequential SBI nested samplers (PolySwyft) now compute evidence. Because the 'simulator' can be the analytic Bianchi template generator, SBI turns a bank of precomputed anisotropic skies into a trained ratio/posterior estimator — the emulator IS the forward model, replacing a bespoke solver entirely.

ammunition.finding: Map-level neural networks now do cosmological model selection directly on CMB temperature+polarization maps, retaining spatial morphology to catch signatures invisible to the power spectrum. ammunition.topic: Imbens-Manski partial-identification confidence intervals: the canonical coverage recipe (and its known non-uniformity fix)
ammunition.finding: Imbens & Manski (2004, Econometrica) constructed confidence intervals that cover the true PARAMETER (not the whole identified set) at fixed probability; they explicitly showed the simplest version does NOT converge uniformly across identification-region widths and modified it to restore uniform coverage. ammunition.topic: Hierarchical/nonparametric inference under selection effects in GW population astronomy: a mature precedent for reporting constrained functionals rather than point detections

Recent nonparametric/model-agnostic extensions (binned Gaussian processes; model-agnostic population frameworks) report flexible, weakly-parametrized population functionals with honest selection modeling, and Essick's 'quick recipes' formalize the selection integral. This is a refereed community precedent for inference that yields calibrated bounds/constraints under strong selection rather than a naive point estimate.

ammunition.topic: Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC): the exact, well-defined replacement for the mislabeled PPC/LOOCV scaffolds
ammunition.finding: SBC (Talts, Betancourt, Simpson, Vehtari & Gelman 2018) validates a Bayesian algorithm by checking that rank statistics of prior draws within posterior draws are uniform; Modrak et al. (2023, Bayesian Analysis) show the choice of test quantity (especially the joint log-likelihood) controls sensitivity to misspecification; Posterior SBC (2025) extends this to data-conditional and amortized settings. SBC is a rigorous, citable calibration standard with an unambiguous definition, distinct from residual/ablation checks.

(2007) inverse-covariance debiasing. Recent covariance-shrinkage work (2026) extends Sellentin-Heavens-type likelihoods for improved stability.

ammunition.topic: Finite-sample calibration of scan/max statistics: the anti-conservative two-stage max-scan is a KNOWN failure with a standard exchangeable-permutation fix
ammunition.finding: Walther & Perry (2020/21) show asymptotic (Gumbel-type) calibrations of scan statistics are too imprecise to control size at practically relevant finite n, and prescribe finite-sample corrections including scale-dependent significance-level adjustment, weighted-Bonferroni scans, and - for exchangeable observations - permutation-based exact calibration. Permutation/conditional-Monte-Carlo tests (Fisher/Pitman lineage) give exact finite-sample size under exchangeability by construction.

ammunition.topic: Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS) as an independent code-verification oracle
ammunition.finding: MMS is the most rigorous general code-verification technique in computational physics: one picks an arbitrary smooth analytic field, substitutes it into the governing PDE/operator to derive the exact source/residual term, then confirms the code reproduces the manufactured field to design order of accuracy. It does NOT require a physically realistic solution and works precisely where closed-form solutions are unavailable (Oberkampf & Roy V&V canon; applied e.g. to verify the BOUT++ plasma-fluid code). This is exactly the 'independent scientific oracle' the audit says schema/smoke tests can never be, because it checks the operator implementation, not I/O plumbing.
references: Oberkampf & Roy 2010, 'Verification and Validation in Scientific Computing' (Cambridge Univ. Press), Ch.5-6 Code/Exact-solutions verification, https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/verification-and-validation-in-scientific-computing/code-verification/733E362E9B977EA1E3745BF9FAF607A0
Dudson et al. 2016, 'Verification of BOUT++ by the Method of Manufactured Solutions', arXiv:1602.06747, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1602.06747

Tao & Boldini et al. (survey) 'Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS)' in computational geomechanics, ScienceDirect S0266352X19302423, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0266352X19302423
ammunition.rescue_leverage: Directly answers the axis-defining rebuke 'No quantity of schema/smoke tests is an independent scientific oracle for estimator bias, coverage, transfer, or masks.' The repo already has a semi-native shear->multipole transfer operator with a saturating 0.632 floor and a PSTF hierarchy; an advocate reframes the D_2 bit-identity anchor and the CAMB visibility cross-check as first steps toward an MMS suite, and proposes manufactured shear/tilt fields with analytically-known low-ell response as the per-lane oracle. This is the concrete deliverable that moves the code axis from 2/5 toward the audit's stated 4/5 gate ('lane-specific independent science oracles').

ammunition.topic: Metamorphic testing and the oracle problem in scientific software
ammunition.finding: Metamorphic testing (MT) alleviates the test-oracle problem by asserting Metamorphic Relations (MRs): known input->output transformation invariances that must hold even when the correct output is unknown (e.g. rotating the sky should rotate a dipole estimate by the same rotation; rescaling distances by lambda should scale a bulk-flow amplitude predictably; adding an isotropic monopole should leave an ell>=2 shear reading invariant). Kanewala & Bieman's systematic review established the oracle problem as the root cause of weak scientific-code testing; MT is now the premier lightweight remedy and has been applied to Monte-Carlo and simulation codes. A 2025 in-depth survey confirms MT/pseudo-oracle/MMS as the standard toolkit for research software.
references: Kanewala & Bieman 2014, 'Testing scientific software: A systematic literature review', Information & Software Technology (also arXiv/ResearchGate 262569275), https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262569275_Testing_Scientific_Software_A_Systematic_Literature_Review

ammunition.topic: Mutation testing to quantify test-suite adequacy (defeating 'false-green')
ammunition.finding: Mutation testing seeds systematic faults ('mutants') into source and measures the fraction the test suite kills (mutation score); it is the premier empirical measure of a suite's fault-revealing power and consistently exposes suites that pass with high coverage but detect no injected bug. Recent work brings this to Python at practical cost (mutmut; hybrid fault-driven mutation; LLM-driven mutation). This is the quantitative rebuttal to a suite that reports green while an estimator is biased.

ammunition.topic: CF4 bulk-flow uncertainty is underestimated -> tension is overestimated (post-Whitford best practice)
ammunition.finding: Whitford, Howlett & Davis (2023) evaluated four bulk-flow estimators (Kaiser MLE, minimum-variance, etc.) against CF4 mocks: the estimators are unbiased in the mean, but their assigned uncertainties are typically underestimated, which mechanically overestimates the tension with LambdaCDM; small residual biases toward low amplitude arise from nonlinear velocities. Watkins et al. (2023) report |B|(200 h^-1 Mpc)=419+/-36 km/s at nominal ~4.8sigma, but the Whitford mock-calibrated errors reduce that significance. Consensus best practice: quote bulk-flow tension ONLY with mock-calibrated covariance, never with the analytic linear-window covariance alone.
